Name: Alcestis
Description: daughter of Pelias and wife of Admetus, who was known for her devotion to her husband

Name: Amymone
Description: the one daughter of Danaus who refused to murder her husband, thus escaping her sisters' punishment

Name: Andromache
Description: wife of Hector

Name: Andromeda
Description: wife of Perseus, who was placed among the constellations after her death

Name: Antigone
Description: daughter of Oedipus and Jocasta

Name: Arachne
Description: a skilled weaver, transformed by Athena into a spider for her blasphemy

Name: Ariadne
Description: daughter of Minos, king of Crete, who aided Theseus in overcoming the Minotaur and became the wife of Dionysus

Name: Atalanta
Description: fleet-footed heroine who participated in the Calydonian Boar hunt

Name: Briseis
Description: a princess of Lyrnessus, taken by Achilles as a war prize

Name: Caeneus
Description: formerly Caenis, a woman who was transformed into a man and became a mighty warrior

Name: Cassandra
Description: a princess of Troy cursed to see the future but never to be believed

Name: Cassiopeia
Description: queen of Æthiopia and mother of Andromeda

Name: Clytemnestra
Description: sister of Helen and unfaithful wife of Agamemnon

Name: Danaë
Description: the mother of Perseus by Zeus

Name: Deianeira
Description: the third wife and unwitting killer of Heracles

Name: Electra
Description: daughter of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra, she aided her brother Orestes in plotting revenge against their mother for the murder of their father

Name: Europa
Description: a Phoenician woman, abducted by Zeus

Name: Hecuba
Description: wife of Priam, king of Troy, and mother of nineteen of his children

Name: Helen
Description: daughter of Zeus and Leda, whose abduction brought about the Trojan War

Name: Hermione
Description: daughter of Menelaus and Helen; wife of Neoptolemus, and later Orestes

Name: Iphigenia
Description: daughter of Agamemnon and Clytemnestra; Agamemnon sacrificed her to Artemis in order to appease the goddess

Name: Ismene
Description: sister of Antigone

Name: Jocasta
Description: mother and wife of Oedipus

Name: Medea
Description: a sorceress and wife of Jason, who killed her own children to punish Jason for his infidelity

Name: Medusa
Description: a mortal woman transformed into a hideous gorgon by Athena

Name: Niobe
Description: a daughter of Tantalus who declared herself to be superior to Leto, causing Artemis and Apollo to kill her fourteen children

Name: Pandora
Description: the first woman

Name: Penelope
Description: loyal wife of Odysseus

Name: Phaedra
Description: daughter of Minos and wife of Theseus

Name: Polyxena
Description: the youngest daughter of Priam, sacrificed to the ghost of Achilles

Name: Semele
Description: mortal mother of Dionysus

Name: Thrace
Description: the daughter of Oceanus and Parthenope, and sister of Europa
